title: Count the price cache's writes the same way for every batch

blocks.text: The price cache is a `TreeMap` from SKU to price in cents, and the cache dashboard plots how many prices callers write. Other code uses the cache as a `NavigableMap`, so it has to stay a `TreeMap`. Prices arrive one at a time through `put`, and in batches through `putAll`: the nightly reload copies yesterday's sorted snapshot into a fresh cache, and the pricing service sends whatever map it has built.

Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/CountingStore.java`, `put` and `putAll`, so that the cache stores prices exactly as a `TreeMap` does and `writes()` counts one write per entry written, overwrites included, for any batch, sorted or not, into an empty cache or a full one. About six lines in total.

cases.says: single writes are stored as a TreeMap stores them and each one is counted, overwrites included
every entry of a batch is stored, in key order, whether the batch is sorted or not
a sorted batch loaded into an empty store counts one write per entry, though TreeMap stores it without calling put
an unsorted batch counts one write per entry, though TreeMap stores it by calling put

origin.section: Code Called Through super Still Calls Your Overrides, So a Subclass Depends on Its Superclass's Self-Calls

concepts: Superclass code reached through super still calls the subclass's overrides, so a subclass that overrides a method its superclass calls on itself depends on the superclass's undocumented implementation.
